text:
Your eyes are tired, poor lover!
Let them remain closed a long while,
in that indolent pose
in which pleasure surprised you.
The murmur of the fountain,
which endures by day and night,
gently prolongs the ecstasy
in which love immersed me.

        The ample jet,
        in a thousand flowers
        where Phoebe shows
        her colors,
        falls like a rain
        of slow tears.

Thus your soul, set ablaze
by the harsh light of joy,
darts bold and swift
toward enchanted skies.
Dying, it changes
into a sad, languid wave
that, down an invisible slope,
plunges into my heart.

        The ample jet,
        in a thousand flowers
        where Phoebe shows
        her colors,
        falls like a rain
        of slow tears.

O you, made beautiful by night,
how sweet it is, against your breast,
to hear the eternal moan
that sobs in the basin!
Water, sound, moon, night,
trees trembling all around,
your pure melancholy
is the mirror of my love.

        The ample jet,
        in a thousand flowers
        where Phoebe shows
        her colors,
        falls like a rain
        of slow tears.

translation.title: The Fountain
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The recurring fountain refrain and its visual indentation are retained.
